outcomes: Taps every square a bishop can reach, including captures and blocked diagonals
Says why a bishop can never reach a square of the other colour
Frees a boxed-in bishop with a pawn move
sources: Rebuilt as a star-grab lesson on 8 Nov 2026 (docs/reach-step.md); wording original.

Bishop movement is a rule of the game; the destination sets and piece squares are claims checked by tools/validate_lessons.py [V]. That a diagonal step keeps the square colour is arithmetic on file and rank [I].
Every reach round is solved by tools/validate_lessons.py (legal moves, par) [V]; the learning effect of moving first is a design bet [I].

steps.say: Slide the bishop to the star.

steps.text: A bishop slides any distance along a **diagonal**: a slanting line of squares that touch at their corners.

steps.say: The king blocks the diagonal. Find a way round.

steps.text: Like the rook, a bishop cannot jump. Its own piece blocks it. It may take an enemy piece by landing there.

steps.say: Take the pawn, then slide on.

steps.text: A bishop always stays on the colour it started on.

steps.caption: Stepping sideways flips the colour, and stepping up flips it again. A diagonal step does both, so the colour never changes.

claims.statement: A white bishop stands on c1.
The bishop can step to d2.
From c1 the bishop reaches exactly these squares, all on its two diagonals.

steps.caption: The c1 bishop is dark, the f1 bishop light. Together they reach every square, so keeping both is usually good; one alone reaches half.

claims.statement: A white bishop stands on the dark square c1.
A white bishop stands on the light square f1.
The bishop on c1 reaches exactly these dark squares.
The bishop on f1 reaches exactly these light squares.

steps.say: Your pawns box the bishop in. Free it, then reach the star.

steps.prompt: Say it back: how does a bishop move, and why can the bishop that starts on c1 never visit a light square?

steps.text: **Model answer.** A bishop slides along diagonals. Each diagonal step flips the colour twice, so the c1 bishop only ever lands on dark squares.

steps.say: One star is light, one is dark. Which bishop can reach which?
